title: Removing Dictionary Items
learningObjectives: Explain removing dictionary items and when it is useful.
Use the relevant Python operations with correct syntax.
Predict the result of common operations and edge cases.
Distinguish mutation, return values and error behavior.
Apply the concept to a small data-processing task.

understand.concept: pop removes a named key and returns its value; popitem removes and returns the most recently inserted pair. del removes a named entry, while clear empties the dictionary. Choose behavior deliberately.
understand.whyItMatters: Removing Dictionary Items is useful when a program needs to organize, inspect or transform related data reliably.
understand.analogy: A dictionary is like a labeled set of drawers: a key identifies the drawer that contains a value.
understand.analogyLimit: A dictionary key is not a physical drawer; keys must be hashable and lookup follows Python's mapping rules.

explain.narrative:
## Removing Dictionary Items

pop removes a named key and returns its value; popitem removes and returns the most recently inserted pair. del removes a named entry, while clear empties the dictionary. Choose behavior deliberately.

## Choosing an operation

Read the example code and check whether the operation mutates the object, returns a new value, or may raise an exception. Use membership tests and defaults where input may be missing.

## Practical reasoning

The five examples progress from basic use to a small real-world pattern. Compare each expected output with the code before changing it.

examples.title: Example 1: Removing Dictionary Items
examples.explanation: del removes the specified key-value pair.

examples.title: Use pop with a default
examples.code:
settings = {'sound': True}
value = settings.pop('language', 'en')
print(value)
print(settings)
examples.explanation: pop returns the default when the key is absent and does not raise KeyError.

examples.title: Remove the last inserted pair
examples.explanation: In modern Python, popitem removes the last inserted pair.

examples.title: Clear all entries
examples.explanation: clear empties the existing dictionary object.

examples.title: Safely remove a possibly absent key
examples.explanation: Check membership before del when absence is possible.
